_comment: Nothing is required here that the template already refuses to render without. The schema catches typos and wrong types; `required` in the template catches an unset value, with a sentence saying why it matters. Each component's `config` is generated into this file from the schema its binary validates against (`just config-schemas`); the rest is written in internal/config/schema/values.base.json.

config-controller-github.description: The configuration of `sluis controller github`: the controller that makes each GitHub organisation's teams match the policy's github table. Secrets are never in this file: a field ending in ...Env holds the NAME of the environment variable that holds the secret, and a field ending in ...File holds a path. Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

console.description: How the controller proves itself to the console, when the pod's `tokenFile` is not the way.

aws.description: The function role's AWS outbound web identity token (`sts:GetWebIdentityToken`), re-minted every four minutes. The console's issuer must federate the account, and its policy must declare an `aws` matcher for the role.

enabledOrgs.description: The organisations the controller changes. Every other bound organisation is derived and reported, and left alone. Each must be one the policy binds.

log.description: Structured logging. One level for the whole service: per-package levels are deliberately not part of the contract.

level.description: The lowest level that is written.

platform.description: What this installation has to build on. The answers pick a preset (the decision tree in docs/design/ports.md), and start refuses an adapter that needs an answer that is no. Absent, the `ports` keys decide and nothing is checked against the platform.

aws.description: AWS is available: its credentials, DynamoDB, S3, SSM, KMS, SQS and EventBridge.

replicas.description: How many replicas share this installation's state. Above 1 start refuses an adapter that keeps its data in the process (`memory`).

runtime.description: Where sluis itself runs. Absent: `kubernetes` with a cluster, else `lambda` on AWS, else `process`.

policyDir.description: The directory the policy is mounted at: the bindings are the policy's github table.

ports.description: The adapters behind the storage ports (docs/design/ports.md).

adapter.description: `legacy` keeps state where it has always been kept: the namespace's ConfigMaps and Secrets and, when `valkey` is set, Valkey. `memory` keeps all of it in this process, which a restart loses: for a local run and the demonstration, and not with `store: kubernetes` or `valkey`.  `dynamodb` keeps the same in one DynamoDB table (`ports.dynamodb`), with the platform's credentials, and takes its Blob from `legacy` unless `ports.blob` names its own.

blob.description: Replaces the Blob port (status reports, directory snapshots) with an adapter of its own, whatever `ports.adapter` is. Absent, the Blob is `ports.adapter`'s.

adapter.description: `s3` keeps the blobs in an S3 bucket.

s3.description: Where the S3 adapter keeps its objects. Credentials are the platform's (EKS Pod Identity, IRSA, a Lambda role) and are never configured here.

bucket.description: The bucket. It must exist, with public access blocked.

endpoint.description: Overrides the S3 address: LocalStack or an S3-compatible store.

kmsKey.description: A KMS key id, ARN or alias for server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) of every write. Absent, the bucket's default encryption applies.

pathStyle.description: Addresses the bucket in the path and not the host name, which LocalStack and most S3-compatible stores need.

prefix.description: A key prefix inside the bucket, for an installation that shares it. Names are `<prefix>/reports/<target>` and `<prefix>/snapshots/<directory>`.

region.description: The bucket's region. Absent, the SDK's own resolution (`AWS_REGION`).

dynamodb.description: The DynamoDB table of the `dynamodb` adapter: one table with a string partition key `pk`, a string sort key `sk` and the TTL attribute `expires`. Credentials are the platform's (EKS Pod Identity, IRSA, a Lambda role) and are never configured here.

create.description: Create the table (on-demand, TTL on `expires`) at start when it is not there, for a test or a development installation. Off, the table must exist: production uses the one the infrastructure code made, and the role needs `dynamodb:DescribeTable` on it.

endpoint.description: Overrides the DynamoDB address: LocalStack or DynamoDB Local.

region.description: The table's region. Absent, the SDK's own resolution (`AWS_REGION`).

preset.description: The adapters of a whole platform, one per concern: `server` (no AWS, no Kubernetes), `k8s-minimal`, `k8s-openbao`, `aws-serverless`, `aws-hybrid` (sluis on Lambda, a cluster for the workloads), `aws-eks`. Absent, the preset the `platform` answers lead to; with neither, the `ports` keys decide. `adapters` and the `ports` keys override single concerns.

probes.description: The health listener. Separate from the service's own traffic, so that readiness is answerable when the service's listener is saturated, and so that a probe is not reachable from outside.

release.description: The name the installation's objects carry. It must be the release's full name: the controller reads the report and the records the service writes under it.

tokenFile.description: This pod's projected ServiceAccount token, presented to the console and read afresh on every call.

adminPasswordEnv.description: The NAME of the variable holding the hub's recovery password, for a run outside a cluster. Unset generates one and prints it once.

allowInsecure.description: Accept a plain-http issuer URL, for a local run.

audience.description: The audience a consumer's token must carry.

consumersFile.description: The file naming the ServiceAccounts that may call it. None named admits nobody in a cluster.

audit.description: The audit installation this service records to. Unset keeps the trail in the log only.

audience.description: The client whose audience the Audit page's tokens carry.

forwardedForTrustedHops.description: How many of the deployment's own proxies append to X-Forwarded-For; zero records the peer.

queryURL.description: The query service, for the console's Audit page. Its own setting: it needs no `writer`, so the page works with the `sqs` and `log` sinks. A path prefix (`https://audit.example/sluis`) is kept and the procedure path appended.

tokenFile.description: This workload's projected service-account token, presented on every call.

clientSecretsDir.description: A directory holding one file per confidential client, named after the client id, each the client's secret. Read per call, so a rotated Secret takes effect without a restart.

cluster.description: Names this cluster in a ServiceAccount's subject. A pod cannot discover it; unset keeps the older unqualified subject.

console.description: Where the console is published, for the sign-in that starts there.

awsAudience.description: The audience an AWS role's web identity token must be minted for to be a bearer at the console (a Lambda controller). Its own, distinct from the AWS federation file's, so a token for token exchange is no proof here and the reverse. Default `<issuerURL>/console`.

client.description: The client id the console signs in as.

origin.description: The console's origin, when it is not the issuer's.

demo.description: Two tenants held in memory, which need no credential and no network.

exchange.description: What the token exchange verifies workloads against.

audience.description: The audience a workload token must be minted for. Defaults to `release`, so two issuers in one cluster cannot accept each other's proofs.

awsFile.description: The file naming the AWS accounts, each by its published key set. Read once at start.

clustersFile.description: The file naming the federated clusters, each by its published key set. Read once at start.

exports.description: The secrets this service copies out of itself into the store `ports.export` names (docs/decisions/0034): a copy is asynchronous, retried with backoff and never a dependency. Validated at start; an unknown source, a source this deployment does not declare and two exports that would write one key stop the service before it serves.

items.description: One copy: what is copied (`source` and the field that names it) and where it goes (`path`, in `namespace`).

app.description: The catalogue id, for `slack-app` and `github-app`. It must be declared in the catalogue.

bundle.description: The bundle, for `bundle`: each is what the Kubernetes Secret of that name held, one JSON document per entry. Written with `replace`: the key holds exactly the bundle.

interval.description: How often the copy is made again with nothing changed, to put back what somebody altered. A change is copied at once; this is the backstop.

name.description: Identifies the export in the log, the metrics and its lease: lower-case letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'. Absent, the source and what it names, e.g. `slack-app.alerts`.

path.description: The key under the KV mount: `slack-apps/alerts`. No leading or trailing slash.

properties.description: Which properties of the App are written and under what names: `{private_key: github-private-key}`. Absent, all of the source's, under the names the External Secrets PushSecrets wrote: `bot_token`; `app_id`, `installation_id`, `private_key`; `github-app-id`, `github-installation-id`, `github-private-key` for a runner App. A property export is a PATCH: other properties of the key are left as they are. Not for `bundle`.

source.description: What is copied. `slack-app`: a catalogue Slack App's bot token (`app`). `github-app`: a catalogue GitHub App's id, installation id and private key (`app`). `runner-app`: a runner App's id, installation id and private key (`tier`, `org`). `bundle`: one of the disaster-recovery bundles, whole (`bundle`).

tier.description: A runner tier, for `runner-app`. It must be one of `github.runnerTiers`.

freshness.description: How the directory's snapshot is kept current.

freshnessWindow.description: How old a snapshot may be and still be answered from.

probeInterval.description: How often the directory is probed.

refreshInterval.description: How often a snapshot is refreshed.

github.description: What the service knows of GitHub.

catalogueFile.description: The file declaring every GitHub App. A malformed one stops the service.

owners.description: The organisations whose repositories' CI tokens are verified. None names none: an empty list would admit every repository there is.

runnerTiers.description: The tiers an operator may create a runner App for: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, at most 16, each once.

groupsScoping.description: How far this installation has moved toward per-audience `groups` scoping: `off`, `report` or `enforce`.

inCluster.description: Prove recovery against the cluster the pod runs in. Set by a deployment that turns recovery on.

issuerURL.description: The issuer: baked into every token and every relying party's trust, so there is no default. No trailing slash is kept.

lifetimes.description: How long what the issuer hands out lives.

absolute.description: A session, at most. Positive, and at least `token`: a session has to end SOMETIME after sign-in, and an access token cannot outlive the session that grants it.

hold.description: How long a removal is held before it takes effect.

session.description: The console's own session cookie, capped at `absolute`.

listen.description: A TCP listener. `address` is a host:port the service binds; an empty host binds every interface.

log.description: Structured logging. One level for the whole service: per-package levels are deliberately not part of the contract.

level.description: The lowest level that is written.

login.description: How a person signs in to the console.

directory.description: Sign in with the corporate directory.

forwarded.description: A sign-in an authenticating proxy has already done.

emailHeader.description: The header that carries the signed-in address.

oauthClient.description: The OAuth client registered once with the directory backend: it drives both admin consent and operator sign-in.

id.description: The client id, for a local run. Not a secret.

idFile.description: A file holding the client id.

idKey.description: The key of the id in that Secret.

secretEnv.description: The NAME of the variable holding the client secret, for a local run.

secretFile.description: A file holding the client secret.

secretKey.description: The key of the secret in that Secret.

secretName.description: The Kubernetes Secret the client is declared in, which the console shows and cannot change.

overlayFile.description: The file of declared workspaces, mounted.

openbao.description: The OpenBao the copies are written to. Nothing is contacted at start: an OpenBao that is down must not stop the service, since a copy is never a dependency.

auth.description: How the service logs in, inside each namespace it writes to. The `kubernetes` and `jwt` methods take the same request (`auth/<mount>/login` with a role and a JWT) and differ in the mount they default to and where the JWT comes from.

method.description: `kubernetes`: the Kubernetes auth method, with this pod's ServiceAccount token. `jwt`: the JWT/OIDC method, with a token the platform projects (a ServiceAccount token of another audience, or, on AWS Lambda, the web identity token of outbound federation) from `tokenFile`.

mount.description: The auth method's mount path in each namespace. Absent, the method's name.

role.description: The role the login asks for. It must be bound to this workload's identity and carry a policy that reads, creates, updates and patches only the paths `exports` names.

tokenFile.description: Where the JWT is read from, afresh on every login. Absent with `kubernetes`, the pod's ServiceAccount token; required with `jwt`.

caFile.description: A PEM bundle of the authorities that sign the server's certificate, in place of the system's.

namespace.description: The OpenBao namespace an export that names none is written to.

publicRootURL.description: The host's root, never carrying the console's mount: the bootstrap surface stays there. Unset follows `publicURL`.

publicURL.description: Where a browser reaches the console, including its mount. The admin-consent redirect URI and the values the setup steps show are built from it. Default http://localhost:8081.

recovery.description: The sign-in that needs no directory: a token for a ServiceAccount, proven against the cluster. Unset is off for the issuer and, for the hub, on.

audience.description: The audience its token must carry.

enabled.description: Turn recovery on. Needs `inCluster`, `serviceAccount` and `audience` to be usable.

serviceAccount.description: The ServiceAccount whose token signs in.

release.description: The name this installation's objects carry: the Kubernetes object names (`<release>-github-orgs`, ...) and the prefix of its keys in a shared store. The chart requires it to be the release's full name.

secureCookies.description: Mark session cookies Secure. Unset follows the scheme the browser will use: https in the URL.

signingKey.description: The issuer's signing keys: provisioned, never minted here.

activationDelay.description: How long a newly published key waits before a replica signs with it. At least `pollInterval`.

additionalFiles.description: Every OTHER algorithm this installation signs with at once, one file per algorithm.

file.description: The primary key. Unset generates one for this process, which a local run may do and nothing else should. Exclusive with `kms`.

kms.description: Sign with AWS KMS keys instead of a file: the private key never leaves KMS. Exclusive with `file`.

additional.description: Every OTHER algorithm this installation signs with at once, each on its own rotation track, as `signingKey.additionalFiles` does for files. RS256 is the one that exists: for relying parties that need it (Kargo, EKS's OIDC provider).

keys.description: RSA_2048, RSA_3072 or RSA_4096 SIGN_VERIFY keys, oldest first, the last signing; same rotation rules as `keys`.

ECC_NIST_P384 SIGN_VERIFY keys, as ids, ARNs or aliases, oldest first. The LAST signs; the earlier ones stay published until `overlap` after the next one activates. Rotation appends a key. The role needs kms:Sign and kms:GetPublicKey on each.

region.description: The keys' region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

stateSecretFile.description: A file holding at least 32 random bytes as base64 or hex (`openssl rand -base64 32`), the same in every replica (a replica whose secret differs refuses to start), from which the sign-in state is derived: a KMS key has no private bytes to derive from.

kmsWrapped.description: Sign with key pairs AWS KMS generates and wraps under ONE symmetric key (the `kms-wrapped` adapter): a new pair per algorithm every `rotateEvery`, published before it signs and kept after it is replaced. The private key is decrypted into process memory to sign. Exclusive with `file` and `kms`.

algorithms.description: The algorithms signed with, the first the installation default. Unset is ES384 and RS256. EdDSA is not supported yet.

keyId.description: The symmetric application key (SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT, ENCRYPT_DECRYPT), as an id, an ARN or an alias. The role needs kms:GenerateDataKeyPairWithoutPlaintext and kms:Decrypt on it, with the encryption context purpose=sluis-signing.

prepublish.description: How long a new key is published before anything signs with it: longer than a verifier caches the key set (Envoy's jwt_authn: 10m). Unset is `activationDelay`.

region.description: The key's region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

retain.description: How long a replaced key stays published: at least `lifetimes.token` plus a skew margin. Unset is `overlap`.

rotateEvery.description: How often a new key pair is generated for each algorithm. Longer than `prepublish`, at most 168h.

stateSecretFile.description: A file holding at least 32 random bytes as base64 or hex, the same in every replica, from which the sign-in state is derived: a wrapped key is replaced daily and the state must outlive it.

overlap.description: How long a rotated key stays published. Unset is `lifetimes.token` plus a margin for clock skew.

pollInterval.description: How often the files are re-read.

slack.description: What the service knows of Slack.

catalogueFile.description: The file declaring every Slack App. A malformed one stops the service.

store.description: Where what an operator connected is kept: `memory` keeps nothing (a restart is a fresh installation), `kubernetes` keeps it in this namespace.

valkey.description: The shared store for logins in progress and snapshots. Unset keeps both in memory, correct for one replica.

cluster.description: Speak the cluster protocol. A plain single server needs it off.

passwordEnv.description: The NAME of the variable holding the password.

config-serve.title: sluis serve

config-serve.envName.description: The NAME of an environment variable: letters, digits and underscores. A value is refused.

config-serve.url.description: An http or https URL with a host and no credentials: a password in a URL is a secret in the file, and a secret is named, never carried.

secretEnv.description: Environment variables from a Secret's keys: the holders of the secrets the config names (`valkey.passwordEnv`, `oauthClient.secretEnv`, `adminPasswordEnv`). A secret is never in `config`.

name.description: The variable, as the config names it.

optional.description: Start without it when the Secret or the key is absent.

secretMounts.description: Secrets mounted read-only as directories, for a file the config names by path (`oauthClient.idFile`, `oauthClient.secretFile`). Each key is a file.

clusterLabel.description: The label that names the cluster on a store that holds several.

interval.description: How often the ruler evaluates the group.

namespace.description: The namespace sluis runs in, whose series the rules read. Empty: the release's.

objectNamespace.description: Where the rule object goes. Empty: the release's namespace.

ruleLabels.description: Labels added to every rule, for Alertmanager routing, such as `k8s_cluster_name`.

failures.description: Failed attempts of one export within `window`.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

exportStale.description: An export has not had its copy in the store for `maxAgeSeconds`.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

issuer5xx.description: The listener answers a share of its requests 5xx.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

minErrors.description: The fewest 5xx in the window that count.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

losses.description: Leases lost within `window` by one kind of target.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

minErrors.description: The fewest failures in the window that count.

ratio.description: The share of calls that failed.

rateLimitLow.description: GitHub's rate-limit budget is nearly spent.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

remaining.description: Requests left under which the alert fires.

seatsShort.description: An organisation has fewer free seats than invitations.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

signingKeyRotationStalled.description: The active signing key is older than `maxAgeSeconds`.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

failures.description: Failed ticks of one target within `window`.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

tickStale.description: A target has had no ok tick for `maxAgeSeconds`.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

tokenLatency.description: The token endpoint's p99 is over `thresholdSeconds`.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

runbookBaseUrl.description: Where the runbook is; the alert's name, lower-cased, is the anchor. Empty renders no link.

audit.description: The projected service-account token this service and the controllers present to the audit installation. The installation itself (`audit.writer` and the rest) is the `config`'s.

audience.description: The audience of the projected token presented to the receiver.

config.description: Rendered as it stands into a ConfigMap and mounted as the file the binary reads with --config. Its schema is serve's: schemas/config/serve.schema.json.

console.description: Where the console is mounted on the issuer's origin. The rest of what the console is configured with is the `config`'s.

mount.description: Where the console is mounted on this issuer's origin, e.g. /console. Empty serves no console.

controllerGithub.description: The GitHub controller (`sluis controller github`): a second process beside the service that makes each organisation's teams match the policy's github table. It runs the chart's one image.

config.description: Rendered as it stands into a ConfigMap and mounted as the file the binary reads with --config. Its schema is controller-github's: schemas/config/controller-github.schema.json.

enabled.description: Render the controller. Needs exchange.clusters to name this cluster and console.mount to be set.

minReadySeconds.description: Seconds a new pod must stay Ready before it counts as available. Default 10.

podDisruptionBudget.description: Rendered only when replicas is above 1.

replicas.description: How many controller pods run. More than one needs the tick leases in a shared State: `config.ports.adapter` of `dynamodb`. The chart refuses it otherwise. Default 1.

strategy.description: The Deployment's rollout. Default RollingUpdate with maxUnavailable 0 and maxSurge 1: the new pod must be Ready before the old one goes.

controllerSlack.description: The Slack controller (`sluis controller slack`): a second process beside the service that makes each workspace's channels match the policy's slack table. It runs the chart's one image.

config.description: Rendered as it stands into a ConfigMap and mounted as the file the binary reads with --config. Its schema is controller-slack's: schemas/config/controller-slack.schema.json.

enabled.description: Render the controller. Needs exchange.clusters to name this cluster and console.mount to be set.

minReadySeconds.description: Seconds a new pod must stay Ready before it counts as available. Default 10.

podDisruptionBudget.description: Rendered only when replicas is above 1.

replicas.description: How many controller pods run. More than one needs the tick leases in a shared State: `config.ports.adapter` of `dynamodb`. The chart refuses it otherwise. Default 1.

strategy.description: The Deployment's rollout. Default RollingUpdate with maxUnavailable 0 and maxSurge 1: the new pod must be Ready before the old one goes.

folder.description: The Grafana folder, for a sidecar that reads the folder annotation.

sidecarLabel.description: The label Grafana's sidecar selects ConfigMaps by.

directory.description: The corporate directories this service reads itself.

push.description: Copy the credential of every connected workspace to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret, for recovery: the whole Secret bundled under one remote key, because the key names inside it are not stable. Absent pushes nothing. deletionPolicy is deliberately not settable -- the case this exists for is the Secret going away.

workspaces.description: Declared workspaces: each names a Secret holding a service-account key and the admin to impersonate.

aws.description: AWS accounts whose IAM roles may exchange their outbound-identity-federation token. Empty verifies none.

jwksUri.description: Where its public keys are. Empty means <issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json.

name.description: The estate's word for the account, for logs.

orgId.description: Require this AWS Organizations id in the token.

audience.description: The audience the role must request from STS. Empty means the issuer's own URL.

maxAge.description: Refuse a token whose iat is older, whatever its exp allows. Default 5m, at most 1h.

clusters.description: Clusters whose workloads may exchange, each verified against the key set that cluster publishes. No secret in any row.

jwksUri.description: Where its public keys are. Empty discovers it from the issuer.

name.description: The estate's word for the cluster; what a workload matcher names.

exports.description: What the chart mounts for the service's exports (docs/decisions/0034): the CA that signs OpenBao's certificate and the projected token the login presents. What is copied and where (`config.exports`), and the OpenBao it is copied to and how the service logs in to it (`config.ports.export`), are the `config`'s.

caBundle.description: PEM of the authorities that sign OpenBao's certificate. Rendered into a ConfigMap and mounted at /var/run/access-issuer/openbao-ca/ca.pem, which `config.ports.export.openbao.caFile` must then be. Empty mounts nothing, and the system's authorities are trusted.

audience.description: The audience of a ServiceAccount token the chart projects at /var/run/openbao/token, for the `jwt` auth method (`config.ports.export.openbao.auth.tokenFile` must then be that path). Empty projects nothing: the `kubernetes` method reads the pod's own ServiceAccount token.

fullnameOverride.description: Replaces the release's full name, the prefix of every object the chart renders and the value `config.release` must carry. An installation migrating from the access-issuer chart sets it to the old full name so no object is renamed.

catalogue.description: GitHub Apps declared as data, created and installed from the console. The service validates the whole catalogue again at start.

push.description: Copy this App's credential to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret: its three property keys only, to the store and path named here. Absent pushes nothing.

Copy the link App and one App per bound organisation to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret, for recovery: the whole Secret bundled under one remote key, because the key names inside it are not stable. Absent pushes nothing. deletionPolicy is deliberately not settable -- the case this exists for is the Secret going away.

nameOverride.description: Replaces the chart name in the `app.kubernetes.io/name` label and in the controllers' selector labels. An installation migrating from the access-issuer chart sets it to access-issuer so the Deployments' immutable selectors are unchanged.

renders.description: What this release renders: `app`, the service and the controllers (the default); `alerts`, only the alert rules; `dashboards`, only the Grafana dashboard ConfigMaps. In the last two nothing else is rendered.

rootRedirect.description: Where a bare GET of the host root goes; empty serves 404.

secretManagers.description: Removed in v1.30.0 — the console's secret-store view was removed. Setting this key fails the render with a clear message. See CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions/0002-mission-boundary-tokens-and-memberships.md.

slackApps.description: Slack Apps declared as data, created and installed from the console. The service validates the whole catalogue again at start, and refuses an entry for a workspace the policy's slack.workspaces does not name.

push.description: Copy this App's bot token to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret: that one key only, to the store and path named here. Absent pushes nothing.

workspace.description: A key of the policy's slack.workspaces.

slackState.description: A recovery copy of the Slack state: see push.

push.description: Copy the credential of every connected Slack workspace, and the mirror of the records that say which workspaces and Slack Connect channels the console holds, to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret, for recovery: each whole Secret bundled under its own remote key (remoteKey for the credentials, recordsRemoteKey for the records), because the key names inside are not stable. Absent pushes nothing. deletionPolicy is deliberately not settable -- the case this exists for is the Secret going away.

telemetry.description: The OpenTelemetry SDK environment on every pod of `renders: app` (ADR 0006). Nothing is rendered without `otlp.endpoint`.

endpoint.description: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: an http(s) URL naming the collector or gateway. Empty: nothing is exported and nothing is rendered.

extraEnv.description: Other OpenTelemetry SDK variables, name to value. Every name starts with OTEL_ and none is OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (checked at render).
